question: What Is the Resonant Frequency of an LC Circuit?
body_html:
LC resonant frequency is the frequency at which inductive reactance equals capacitive reactance, so the two cancel and energy swings between L and C.

f0 = 1 / (2π√(LC))

Example: L = 100 µH and C = 100 pF give √(LC) = 0.1 µs, so f0 = 1591.55 kHz, about 1.6 MHz. With 10 Ω series resistance, Q = (1 / R) × √(L / C) = 100 and bandwidth = f0 / Q = 15.92 kHz.
